title: Pattern Separation vs Completion
content_html:
Pattern Separation vs Completion

EC inputs are decorrelated by DG (pattern separation) and conveyed via mossy fibers to CA3, whose recurrent collaterals support attractor dynamics for pattern completion. CA1/subiculum route information back to neocortex.

Why this matters for memory

Reduce interference (encoding): DG separation ensures similar episodes form distinct traces, protecting them from mutual interference.
Robust recall (retrieval): CA3 completion rebuilds whole memories from partial/noisy cues.
Balanced generalization: Too much separation → fragmentation; too much completion → overgeneralization/false memories. Neuromodulators and task demands tune this balance.
